newsitem.title: USA: US NASD forms task force to aid criminal probes.
newsitem.headline: US NASD forms task force to aid criminal probes.

text.p: The National Association of Securites Dealers has formed a task force to coordinate efforts with law enforcement officials, a NASD letter released Tuesday said.

"The task force will aid criminal authorities taking part in investigations and undercover operations involving the securities industry," Mary Schapiro, president of NASD Regulation, wrote in a Feb. 28 letter to Michigan Democrat Rep. John Dingell.

"What we can bring to the criminal enforcement table is the necessary and technical expertise for government law enforcement agencies to conduct significant and effective criminal investigations," Schapiro wrote in the letter.

Early last month, Dingell wrote to U.S. Attorney General Janet Reno and to the Securities and Exchange Commission and NASD to ask what they are doing about alleged organized crime infiltration of the small-capital stock market.
SEC Chairman Arthur Levitt responded at end-February by offering Dingell, the House Commerce Committee ranking member, a confidential briefing on the allegations.

In the letter, Schapiro also offered a private briefing to discuss several ongoing senstive matters related to the NASD's work with the Organized Crime Unit of the FBI and other federal law enforcement agencies.

NASD also entered into and is negotiating a number of Memoranda of Understanding with federal law enforcement agencies that involve investigations of registered entities having possible connections to organized crime, Schapiro said.
Schapiro said she offered to brief Dingell privately about the details of the MOUs and the nature of the continuing investigations, including undercover operations.

NASD Regulation is regulatory arm of the National Association of Securities Dealers, a trade group for the U.S. financial industry. NASD is also the self-regulatory agency that runs the Nasdaq stock market.

A Dec. 16 Business Week article said a three-month investigation showed "substantial elements of the small-cap market have been turned into a vertible mob franchise, under the very noses of regulators and law enforcement."

In her letter to Dingell, Schapiro said prior to the publication, NASD had "significant ongoing investigations of our own involving all but one of the member firms and many of the nineteen Nasdaq or OTC (Over The Counter) Bulletin Board issuers mentioned in the article."
Since publication of the article, NASD initiated an investigation of the one remaining firm and conducted a review of trading activity in the remaining securities, she said.
The member firms and issuers were not named in the letter.
